long_biography.plain_text:
Gușa de Drăgan joined the Drăgan Group in 1997 as a board member and rose to executive president and managing director before her husband, ButanGas founder Iosif Constantin Drăgan, died. That progression gave her an operating role years before succession. She also established the General Ștefan Gușă Foundation, linking her business life with education and historical research.

After inheriting Drăgan’s business interests, she created Veroniki Holding in Milan in 2010 to centralize strategy, finance and control across the family group. LPG distribution remained the core business, while the portfolio expanded through renewable energy, real estate, healthcare and food packaging. As chairwoman and managing director, she has overseen a European network while backing educational institutions and a major oncology-surgery donation.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at 100 through the distinctive compound surname, Romanian birth context, Italian business base, Veroniki and ButanGas leadership, and exact official birth record. No private-asset assertion is used as the public identity bridge.

The canonical public order is Daniela Veronica, not the source's Veronica Daniela. Official Romanian usage also supports Gușa de Drăgan with diacritics as one compound surname. The source title field separately contains Dr., so the apply-ready display correction removes the duplicated embedded honorific while retaining the separate supported title.

Official company materials use Dr. or Dott.ssa and identify Gușa de Drăgan as a law graduate. The dossier preserves the separate title but does not describe it as proof of a research doctorate or PhD.

The Luxembourg official gazette gives 12 July 1973 in Turda, Cluj, correcting the saved 1974 year. Independent reporting describing her as 46 in November 2019 corroborates 1973, while no equally strong source supports 1974.

WIPO's natural-person holder-nationality code identifies Spain, and Romanian registry-based reporting separately calls her a Spanish citizen. Spanish is therefore proposed as a secondary nationality without replacing the saved Romanian nationality. Historical Spanish residence is not proposed because the source already records current main residence in Italy.

Inheritance is directly documented rather than inferred from marriage: Profit.ro attributes her fortune to assets inherited from Iosif Constantin Drăgan, and Ziarul Financiar describes her as his heiress. No private estate percentage, trust mechanism or distribution among family members is asserted.

ButanGas was founded by Iosif Constantin Drăgan in 1948. Gușa de Drăgan entered the group later, led it before succession, inherited business interests, and founded Veroniki Holding in 2010; Founder is therefore not used as her wealth relationship to the underlying fortune.

Official and independent sources differ on whether her executive presidency began in 2001 or 2003. The biographies say only that she attained senior leadership before her husband's 2008 death, which both chronologies support.

Energy is both the wealth-creation and current-primary industry because LPG distribution remains the group's stated core business. Renewable energy, real estate, healthcare, shipping and food packaging are meaningful extensions but do not displace the LPG-led platform as primary.

Operator describes her sustained group leadership before and after succession. Inherited and expanded captures the documented spousal transfer plus subsequent consolidation and diversification without attributing her husband's original ButanGas creation to her.

Oil & gas is the sole minimum-useful active tag. Renewable energy is a substantial secondary activity, but the broader current grouping remains anchored in LPG distribution and adding a second sector tag is unnecessary for this dossier.

No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, TikTok or personal website cleared the verification threshold. The dedicated Forbes page and exact current employer-governance page are proposed under supported type IDs.

The source record's personally associated craft names, private ownership records, specifications and cohort rank were used only for identity disambiguation and are excluded from biography, wealth classifications, tags and proposals.
